header: Structure advice for {path}. Each point needs your decision, and no point blocks your work. Consider each point with care. An ignored point can lower the quality and cohesion of the codebase, and make the work of future agents harder.
crowded-folder: The folder of {path} holds {count} files. The folder limit is {limit}. Its name families are: {families}. Its import groups are: {components}. A crowded folder makes the next reader or agent search many files for one part. Which group does {path} join? Move that group into a sub-folder now. Or, if you keep the layout, give the reason in one line of your GREEN report.
name-stem-cluster: The folder of {path} holds {count} files whose names start with {stem}: {examples}. Similar names, with no folder of their own, make the next reader or agent guess which file does what. Does the {stem} group need its own sub-folder? Move the group into a sub-folder now. Or, if you keep the layout, give the reason in one line of your GREEN report.
generic-name: {path} has the generic name {stem}. A generic name does not show the job of the file, so the next reader or agent must open the file to know what it holds. What name shows the job of {path}? Rename the file now to that name. Or, if you keep the name, give the reason in one line of your GREEN report.
boundary-edge: Line {line} of {path} breaks a boundary rule of the {from_context} context: {text}. The rule is: {rule}. A reference across a context boundary lets one change break the other context. Which fix fits this reference? Use the public interface of the other context, or move the code to a shared folder. Or, if the rule is out of date, say so in one line of your GREEN report.
